question: Should OpenClaw add a supported config path that disables Control UI token URL auth and also relaxes HTTPS, device identity, pairing, and tailnet trust checks for private or tailnet deployments?
rationale: The requested behavior intentionally weakens Gateway authentication and device trust boundaries, and current code/docs preserve those as explicit security controls rather than missing implementation.

options.title: Keep Current Boundaries
options.body: Maintain token/password, trusted-proxy, verified Tailscale identity, and explicit break-glass behavior as the supported paths unless a narrower security design is sponsored.

options.title: Sponsor Dangerous Opt-In
options.body: Design a named private-ingress or tailnet opt-in with clear warnings, audit findings, docs, startup validation, and tests for every relaxed boundary.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: If maintainers reject this trust model, close this and the overlapping auth-none request with guidance toward trusted-proxy, token/password, or verified Tailscale Serve paths.

recommendation.title: Keep Current Boundaries
recommendation.body: Maintain token/password, trusted-proxy, verified Tailscale identity, and explicit break-glass behavior as the supported paths unless a narrower security design is sponsored.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties this handle to Gateway auth hardening and the current no-auth Tailscale exposure boundary.
